rationale: The pattern is applied to the local date command output before emitting a millisecond timestamp. No untrusted field reaches this check.
The value comes from the receiver-local server-to-shell timing record, not from a request field; the security and protocol checks live in the authenticated server and the action parser.
The compared current time comes from the local clock helper. This is internal timing evidence, not a security-boundary input.
WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENV is operator configuration. The exact function checks the Bash identifier grammar before indirect expansion; the same contract will replay both resolve and clear paths.
This is the second occurrence of the same environment-name guard in the clear helper. It is covered by the line-167 contract and gate rather than counted as another independent question.

The helper combines an ASCII digit regex with Bash numeric comparison. The docs do not state whether leading-zero decimal text is valid; Bash arithmetic treats such values specially, so the product domain is unresolved.

The exact helper validates remote webhook-derived owner/repository text before it enters invalidation calls or the PROCESS_PR action. The adjacent owner-start and dot-name checks are part of this whole-helper contract.
This adjacent regex is a required subcheck of the line-197 repository-slug contract, not an independent product property.
The exact helper checks the SHA-shaped request-derived value before passing it to the cache invalidator. This is a downstream guard; the server also validates the field.
The action record is emitted by the pinned local Python server from its own receive timestamp. This line validates the local protocol record and is not an external-input boundary.

The dispatcher only calls process_pr after parsing an action record and validating its remote-event-derived slug and positive decimal PR number. The server authenticates and parses the webhook first; this is a final shell-side protocol guard.
